title: Kepler's third law in exoplanet systems
summary: Planets orbit stars; the orbit's period and size, with the star's mass, obey P² = a³/M★. The catalogue mixes measured and computed values.

concepts.label: Planetary system
concepts.description: A star with one or more planets.

children.label: Stellar mass
children.description: M★ in solar masses, from spectra and stellar evolution models.

children.label: Exoplanet
children.description: A planet outside the Solar System.

children.label: Semi-major axis
children.description: Half the long axis of the elliptical orbit (AU).

children.label: Discovery method
children.description: Transit, radial velocity, imaging, microlensing, timing.

children.label: Planet mass
children.description: Neglected here; adds to M★ in the exact law.

concepts.label: Kepler's third law
concepts.description: P² = 4π²a³/(G(M★+m)); in years, AU and solar masses P² = a³/M★.

facts.text: Kepler published the harmonic law in Harmonices Mundi (1619); Newton derived it from gravitation in the Principia (1687).

children.label: Dynamical mass
children.description: The central mass a³/P² implied by an orbit.

children.label: Transit stellar density
children.description: (a/R★)³/P² from the light curve's shape: a law-based measurement that needs no stellar mass.

concepts.label: Data provenance
concepts.description: Which paper each value comes from, and whether it was measured or derived.

children.label: Per-reference solutions
children.description: The archive's ps table: one row per planet and paper.
